literal: Virtue he speaks not, evil things even if he does, a person 'back he speaks not' saying is sweet.
translation: Even if a person does not speak of virtue and commits evil deeds, it is good to be able to say that he does not backbite.
modern: ஒருவன் அறத்தைப் பற்றிப் பேசாமல் பாவச் செயல்களைச் செய்தாலும், அவன் மற்றவர்களைப் பற்றிப் புறம் பேசமாட்டான் என்று சொல்லப்படுவது அவனுக்கு நல்லதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the severe nature of backbiting by comparing it to other moral failings. It states that even if someone completely ignores virtuous speech and actively commits bad deeds, refraining from speaking ill behind others' backs remains a redeeming quality. The word 'புறம்' refers to the back, meaning speaking behind someone's back. The poet suggests that avoiding this specific flaw brings a distinct sweetness or goodness ('இனிது') to a person's character.
